mainTopic: Fixing a broken harp string in the מקדש on שבת, and when a wart may be cut off for the מקדש service on שבת.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a לוי's harp string that tore on שבת. The משנה allows tying it with a knot, but a ברייתא allows only a bow. The גמרא gives three answers: it is a מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the רבנן; or both follow the רבנן and it depends on whether the string tore in the middle or at the side; or both speak of a tear in the middle and they argue about making a גזירה. Then a new משנה teaches that a wart may be cut off by hand in the מקדש on שבת, but not elsewhere, and never with a tool. The גמרא contrasts this with a משנה in פסחים that says cutting the wart of the קרבן פסח does not override שבת. Two אמוראים answer: either hand versus tool, or moist versus dry, and each defends his answer against the other. רב יוסף rejects the hand-versus-tool answer and says a שבות for the מקדש is permitted inside the מקדש but not out in the country. רב ספרא challenges this with a scroll on a threshold and with the פסח in the oven, and the גמרא answers both. Finally, רבא explains that our משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who still requires doing the act in a changed way, by hand.

steps.title: The answer based on רבי אליעזר does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier idea that the source allowing only a bow follows רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר would allow even more than that, even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was speaking according to רבי אליעזר, then it should be allowed even from the start (לכתחילה) too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is knocking down the answer it just tried. That answer said the source permitting a bow follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that the preparations needed for a מצוה override שבת. So by his view there would be no reason to limit things to an after-the-fact bow; he would allow it לכתחילה. Since the source is limited, it cannot be following רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is according to (the view of)
From the start, as the preferred way of acting
Also, too

phrases.english: If he is speaking according to Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: Refers back to the answer the גמרא proposed on the previous amud.

phrases.english: then even from the start it should also be permitted!
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר permits the preparations for a מצוה on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קָאָמַר, אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִילָּה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the previous (pre-passage) answer that tied the source to רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attribution of the limited ruling to רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's view is too lenient to explain a ruling that only allows something בדיעבד.

steps.title: New answer: the sources follow רבי שמעון and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The source that forbids a knot follows רבי שמעון. The משנה that permits a knot follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: this one follows רבי שמעון, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: After throwing out the רבי אליעזר answer, the גמרא gives a fresh answer. It says the two sources follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that allows only a bow (no knot) follows the stricter view of רבי שמעון. The משנה that allows tying a knot follows the more lenient רבנן. So the two sources are not really contradicting each other; they reflect a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals dropping the old answer for a new one)
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one ... that one

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this (baraita) follows Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: The source that permits only a bow.

phrases.english: that (mishna) follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The source that permits tying a knot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא — רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the two sources contradict, or that one follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון (only a bow); the משנה follows the רבנן (a knot is allowed).

steps.title: Proof: a ברייתא where רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree about the harp string
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת directly. The רבנן allow the לוי to tie a knot, while רבי שמעון allows only a bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A לוי whose harp string tore may tie it. רבי שמעון says: he may only make a bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that this exact מחלוקת really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed first opinion (the רבנן) permits a real knot. This matches the משנה. רבי שמעון permits only a bow, matching the other ברייתא. This confirms the answer in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: A string (of a musical instrument)
Harp, lyre
He ties it with a knot
He ties it with a bow (a loose loop)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up קשירה (a real knot, which is a מלאכה) with עניבה (a bow, which is more lenient). The whole מחלוקת depends on this difference.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
A Levite for whom there tore
phrases.notes: Refers to the לויים who played music in the מקדש.

phrases.english: a string on the harp may tie it with a knot;
phrases.notes: This is the view of the Rabbis (the first, unnamed opinion).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: he may only form a bow.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה לוֹ נִימָא בְּכִנּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree about tying a knot versus a bow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a לוי's torn harp string.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: neither a knot nor a bow works, so rewind the string
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a third view. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a tied string will not sound right, so one should rewind the string from the pegs instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even that will not make the proper sound. Rather, he lets out the string from the bottom and winds it at the top, or lets it out from the top and winds it at the bottom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא, which adds a third opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר argues that tying, whether with a knot or a bow, ruins the sound. Then the person would break שבת without properly doing the מצוה. So he suggests a different fix: loosen the string from one peg and wind the extra length around the other peg until it is tight again.

keyTerms.meaning: Produces the (proper) sound
Lets out, unwinds
Winds around

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הִיא אֵינָהּ מַשְׁמַעַת אֶת הַקּוֹל.
phrases.english: Even it (a tied string) does not produce the proper sound.
phrases.notes: So tying would break שבת without properly doing the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, he unwinds (the string) from below
phrases.notes: From the lower peg.

phrases.english: and winds it around above,
phrases.notes: Around the upper peg.

phrases.english: or he unwinds from above
and winds it around below.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף הִיא אֵינָהּ מַשְׁמַעַת אֶת הַקּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא brought in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tying ruins the sound, so the string is fixed by rewinding it from one peg onto the other.

steps.title: Second answer: both follow the רבנן; middle versus side
steps.stepSummary: Both sources can follow the רבנן. The difference depends on where the string tore: in the middle, a knot is allowed; near the side, a bow is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both this and that follow the רבנן, and it is not difficult. Here it tore in the middle; there it tore at the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to answer the contradiction. This time it does not split the sources between different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the string tore in the middle, a bow would ruin the sound, so the משנה allows a real knot. If it tore near the end, a bow works fine, so the ברייתא allows only a bow. Both rulings fit the רבנן, who permit needed preparations for the מצוה but no more than necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
Both this and that
Here ... there (distinguishing two cases)
In the middle
At the side, near the end

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. A contradiction can be solved either by assigning the sources to different תנאים or by applying them to different cases, here based on what is actually needed for the מצוה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that follow the Rabbis,
and it is not difficult:
here, where it tore in the middle,
phrases.notes: The משנה allows a knot, since a bow would ruin the sound.

phrases.english: there, where it tore at the side.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא allows only a bow, since a bow is enough there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the answer in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the two sources must reflect a מחלוקת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow the רבנן: a knot when the string tore in the middle, a bow when it tore at the side.

steps.title: Third answer: both sources speak of a tear in the middle, and they argue about a precaution
steps.stepSummary: A third way to settle the two sources about the torn string. Both speak of a tear in the middle. רבי שמעון forbids a knot there as a precaution, and the רבנן do not make that precaution.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: both sources speak of a string that tore in the middle. One Sage holds we make a precaution. The other Sage holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third answer to the same contradiction about tying the torn string. It goes back to the idea that the two sources reflect a real disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said both sources follow the רבנן and that the case is different: middle versus side. This answer says the case is the same (a tear in the middle), and the two sources really disagree. רבי שמעון forbids a knot even in the middle, so that people will not also tie a knot on the side where it is not needed. The רבנן do not make that precaution.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say...': introduces an alternative answer
In the middle (of the string)
We make a rabbinic precaution (גזירה)
'One Sage holds': introduces each side of a disagreement

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to settle the torn-string sources. (1) It is a מחלוקת: רבי שמעון allows only a bow, while the רבנן allow a knot. (2) Both follow the רבנן, and the difference is where it tore: middle means a knot, side means a bow. (3) Both speak of a tear in the middle, and רבי שמעון makes a גזירה while the רבנן do not.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
phrases.notes: Signals a third, alternative answer.

phrases.english: both this and that are where it tore in the middle,
one Sage holds: we make a precaution,
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון in the ברייתא: no knot even in the middle, lest one tie at the side.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: we do not make a precaution.
phrases.notes: These are the רבנן in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from step 5's split between middle and side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Real disagreement over a rabbinic precaution, in the same case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 5: both follow the רבנן, and the two sources speak of different tear locations.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both speak of a tear in the middle. רבי שמעון makes a גזירה and the רבנן do not.

steps.title: New משנה: cutting off a wart on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a wart may be cut off in the מקדש on שבת, but not elsewhere. With a tool, it is forbidden everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We cut off a wart in the מקדש, but not in the rest of the country. If it is done with a tool, it is forbidden both here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches a rule about removing a wart on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wart is a blemish (מום) that makes a כהן or a קרבן unfit until it is removed. In the מקדש, the rabbinic שבת restrictions were relaxed to let the עבודה go on, so removing the wart by hand is allowed there. Outside the מקדש there is no such need, so it is forbidden. Using a tool is a more serious kind of cutting, so it stays forbidden even in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A wart; a blemish that makes a כהן or a קרבן unfit
The Temple
The rest of the country, outside the מקדש
A tool or instrument
The משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the string discussion above. This is a brand-new משנה on a new topic.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
We cut off a wart in the Temple,
phrases.notes: Meaning by hand, to make a כהן or a קרבן fit.

phrases.english: but not in the rest of the country.
And if it is done with a tool,
it is forbidden both here and there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting off a wart by hand is allowed on שבת in the מקדש but not outside it. With a tool, it is forbidden everywhere.

steps.title: Contradiction from the פסח משנה: cutting a wart does not push aside שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in פסחים: carrying the קרבן פסח, bringing it from beyond the תחום, and cutting off its wart do not push aside שבת. רבי אליעזר says they do. This seems to contradict our משנה, which allows cutting a wart in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And they contrasted it with this: carrying it, bringing it from outside the תחום, and cutting off its wart do not push aside שבת. רבי אליעזר says: they do push it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. Another משנה seems to forbid exactly what our משנה permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a wart may be cut off in the מקדש on שבת. The משנה in פסחים says cutting the wart of the קרבן פסח does not push aside שבת. Only רבי אליעזר permits it. So the main view there seems to clash with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted it': introduces a contradiction from another source
Carrying it (the animal) on one's shoulders
The שבת boundary one may not walk beyond
They push aside (override) שבת

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they contrasted it with this:
carrying it, and bringing it from outside the Shabbat boundary,
phrases.notes: Speaking of the קרבן פסח when ערב פסח falls on שבת.

phrases.english: and cutting off its wart do not override Shabbat,
Rabbi Eliezer says: they do override!
phrases.notes: This fits רבי אליעזר's well-known view that steps needed to prepare a מצוה override שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to cut off a wart in the מקדש on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in פסחים says cutting a קרבן's wart does not override שבת (except for רבי אליעזר). That contradicts our משנה, which allows it.

steps.title: First answer: both speak of a moist wart; hand is allowed, a tool is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בן חנינא answer in two ways. One says both sources speak of a moist wart. Our משנה allows it by hand, and the פסחים משנה forbids it with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בן חנינא: one said both speak of a moist wart, and there is no difficulty. Here it is by hand; there it is with a tool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the contradiction. Two אמוראים disagree on how to answer it, and this is the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a moist wart by hand is not the normal way to do it, so it is only forbidden by the רבנן. In the מקדש, rabbinic restrictions were not applied, so our משנה permits it. The פסחים משנה speaks of using a tool, which is forbidden by the תורה, so it does not override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist (a wart that is still fresh, not dried out)
'One said': introduces one of two unnamed opinions
'And it is not difficult': introduces a resolution
By hand

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'כאן' (by hand) refers to our משנה in עירובין. The second 'כאן' (with a tool) refers to the משנה in פסחים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei ben Ḥanina disagree:
one said:
both this and that speak of a moist wart,
and it is not difficult:
here it is by hand, there it is with a tool.
phrases.notes: By hand is only a rabbinic prohibition, so it is allowed in the מקדש. With a tool is a תורה prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בְּלַחָה, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to argue about the same act of cutting a wart.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה permits removal by hand, which is only rabbinically forbidden. The פסחים משנה forbids removal with a tool, which is forbidden by the תורה.

steps.title: Second answer: both by hand, moist versus dry
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says both sources speak of removing the wart by hand. The משנה in פסחים forbids a moist wart, and our משנה allows a dry one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: both cases are by hand, and there is no difficulty. This one is about a moist wart, and that one is about a dry wart.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second of the two answers from רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי בן חנינא. It settles the contradiction between our משנה and the משנה in פסחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer split the sources by how the wart is removed: by hand or with a tool. This answer keeps both sources about the hand and splits them by the kind of wart instead. Cutting a moist wart, which is still living tissue, is forbidden. A dry wart is already dying and almost falling off, so removing it is a lighter matter that our משנה permits in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one said. It introduces the second of two answers.
Moist. A wart that is still fresh and connected to living skin.
Dry. A wart that has dried out and is almost falling off.
By hand, without a tool

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. In the first answer, both sources speak of a moist wart, and the difference is hand versus tool. In this answer, both sources speak of the hand, and the difference is moist versus dry.

phrases.english: And the other one said: both this and that are by hand,
and it is not difficult:
this one is about a moist wart,
phrases.notes: The משנה in פסחים, which forbids it

phrases.english: that one is about a dry wart.
phrases.notes: Our משנה, which permits it in the מקדש

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בַּיָּד, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two answers that were introduced in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different case (dry wart versus moist wart)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to argue about whether a wart may be cut for the קרבן on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both speak of removing by hand. A moist wart is forbidden and a dry wart is permitted in the מקדש.

steps.title: Why didn't the first אמורא split by moist and dry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the אמורא who split by hand and tool did not use the simpler moist-versus-dry answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who said 'this is by hand and that is with a tool,' what is the reason he did not say 'this is moist and that is dry'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the two answers. It asks why the first אמורא did not accept the second אמורא's way. This sets up an explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two אמוראים give different answers, the גמרא often asks why each one rejected the other's answer. This is not an attack. It is a request to find the reason behind each choice.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who said. It introduces a question about one specific opinion.
What is the reason he did not say. It asks why a scholar avoided another answer.
A tool or instrument

phrases.english: And according to the one who said, 'This is by hand, that is with a tool,'
what is the reason he did not say
'This is moist, that is dry'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָא בַּיָּד הָא בִּכְלִי מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers and asks why the first אמורא did not choose the second
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the hand-versus-tool אמורא rejected the moist-versus-dry answer

steps.title: A dry wart may be removed even with a tool
steps.stepSummary: He holds that a dry wart may be removed even with a tool, because it is already crumbling. So moist versus dry cannot explain our משנה, which forbids a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can say to you: a dry wart is permitted even with a tool. What is the reason? It is crumbling away anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first אמורא rejected the moist-versus-dry answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, a dry wart is like dead skin that is already falling apart. Removing it is permitted even with a tool. But our משנה says that with a tool it is forbidden everywhere. So our משנה cannot be talking about a dry wart, and the moist-versus-dry split does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you. It introduces a scholar's defense of his own view.
It is permitted
It is crumbling away. It is already falling apart by itself.

phrases.english: He can say to you: a dry wart,
even with a tool, it is also permitted.
What is the reason? It is crumbling away.
phrases.notes: Removing it is like peeling off dead skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: יְבֵישָׁה אֲפִילּוּ בִּכְלִי נָמֵי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dry wart is permitted even with a tool, so our משנה's ban on a tool must refer to a moist wart.

steps.title: Why didn't the second אמורא split by hand and tool?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the reverse question: why did the moist-versus-dry אמורא not use the hand-versus-tool answer?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who said 'this is moist and that is dry,' what is the reason he did not say 'this is by hand and that is with a tool'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the second אמורא. This sets up his reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 11. Now the גמרא wants to know what was wrong, in the second אמורא's eyes, with the first answer.

phrases.english: And according to the one who said, 'This is moist and that is dry,'
what is the reason he did not say
'This is by hand, that is with a tool'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָא בְּלַחָה וְהָא בִּיבֵישָׁה מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reverse of the question in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the moist-versus-dry אמורא rejected the hand-versus-tool answer

steps.title: Our משנה already forbids a tool
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה already says plainly that a tool is forbidden everywhere. So the משנה in פסחים would have no reason to teach that again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can say to you: about a tool, we already learned, 'If with a tool, it is forbidden here and there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second אמורא rejected the hand-versus-tool answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה in פסחים were only teaching that a tool is forbidden, it would be repeating something our משנה already states clearly. A משנה is not expected to teach the same thing twice for no reason. So the משנה in פסחים must be teaching something new, such as a ban on a moist wart even by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: But we already learned. It points to an existing משנה that already teaches this.
It is forbidden here and there, meaning both in the מקדש and outside it

phrases.english: He can say to you: about a tool,
we already learned it:
'If with a tool, here and there it is forbidden.'
phrases.notes: Quoted from our משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on a tool is already explicit in our משנה, so the משנה in פסחים would be repeating it for no reason.

steps.title: The משנה in פסחים repeats it to show רבי אליעזר's disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The hand-versus-tool אמורא answers back. The משנה in פסחים repeats the case of a tool only to record that רבי אליעזר disagrees with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? What is taught there is taught because it wants to show the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The first אמורא defends himself against the point raised in step 14. The next steps continue the back-and-forth between the two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in פסחים is not just repeating a rule. It needs to name the case so that it can show that רבי אליעזר permits even cutting with a tool. The repetition has a new purpose, so it is not extra, and the hand-versus-tool answer still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one. It asks how the other scholar would respond.
To show a disagreement between scholars

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the wart. Answer 1: both are moist; by hand is allowed and with a tool is forbidden. Answer 2: both are by hand; dry is allowed and moist is forbidden. Each אמורא has a reason to reject the other. The first holds that dry is fine even with a tool. The second holds that the tool ban is already taught. The first answers back that the משנה in פסחים repeats it to show רבי אליעזר's disagreement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a rule that seems repeated is explained as needed to set up a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: And the other one?
This that it teaches there,
is because it wants
to show the dispute of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ הָא דְּקָתָנֵי הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי אִיפְּלוֹגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the point raised in step 14 against the hand-versus-tool answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repetition has a purpose: it sets up a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in פסחים would be needlessly repeating the ban on a tool.
steps.terutzMaskana: It repeats the case in order to record that רבי אליעזר permits it, so it is not extra.

steps.title: The wart case is grouped with rabbinic cases
steps.stepSummary: The moist-versus-dry אמורא pushes back. The משנה in פסחים lists the wart next to carrying the animal and bringing it from outside the תחום, which are only רבנן-level. So the wart case there must also be רבנן-level, meaning by hand and not with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: the wart case is taught alongside carrying the animal and bringing it from outside the תחום, which are only forbidden by the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The moist-versus-dry אמורא rejects the claim that the משנה in פסחים is talking about a tool. He points to the other cases listed next to the wart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה in פסחים, the wart is listed with carrying the animal and bringing it from outside the תחום. Those two are only forbidden by the רבנן. Cases listed together should be at the same level, so the wart case must be cutting by hand (a רבנן-level rule), not with a tool (a תורה-level rule).

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other אמורא)
Similar to, parallel to
Carrying it (the animal on one's shoulders)
The שבת boundary
Forbidden only by the רבנן

phrases.english: And the other one (says):
phrases.notes: The moist-versus-dry אמורא answers back

phrases.english: Similar to carrying it and bringing it
phrases.notes: The other cases in the משנה in פסחים

phrases.english: from outside the boundary it is taught, which are rabbinic.
phrases.notes: So the wart case must also be rabbinic, meaning by hand

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 15's claim that the משנה in פסחים speaks of a tool
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the משנה in פסחים deals with cutting by tool
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wart is listed next to rabbinic cases, so it too must be a rabbinic case (by hand)

steps.title: The other listed cases can be תורה-level
steps.stepSummary: The hand-versus-tool אמורא answers that carrying and bringing from outside the תחום can be תורה-level too. Carrying is תורה-level if we do not follow רבי נתן. The תחום is תורה-level according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: carrying the animal is תורה-level, because the משנה does not follow רבי נתן, who says a living creature carries itself. Bringing it from outside the תחום is תורה-level, because the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who says the תחום rules come from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The hand-versus-tool אמורא defends himself. He shows that the cases next to the wart can also be Torah-level, so a tool case fits in that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן holds that a living being 'carries itself', so carrying an animal is only a רבנן-level problem. The משנה can follow the view that argues with him, which makes carrying a תורה-level problem. רבי עקיבא holds that the תחום comes from the תורה. With that, all three cases can be תורה-level, and cutting with a tool fits right in.

keyTerms.meaning: A living being carries itself, so carrying it is not Torah-level carrying
From the Torah (Torah-level)

phrases.english: And the other one (says):
phrases.notes: The hand-versus-tool אמורא

phrases.english: Carrying it is not according to רבי נתן,
who said: a living being carries itself.
Bringing it from outside the boundary is according to רבי עקיבא,
who said: boundaries are from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against step 16 by making the other listed cases Torah-level
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching the משנה to specific תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cases next to the wart are only רבנן-level, so the wart case must be by hand
steps.terutzMaskana: All the listed cases can be Torah-level, so a tool case fits in the list

steps.title: רבי אליעזר calls these cases שבות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects using רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר. רבי אליעזר calls these actions שבות, which means they are only רבנן-level. That knocks out the claim that they are תורה-level.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: רבי אליעזר said, this is a קל וחומר. Slaughtering is a תורה-level מלאכה, and it still overrides שבת. These actions are only שבות. Surely they should override שבת too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to challenge step 17. In the same משנה in פסחים, רבי אליעזר calls these actions שבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's whole argument depends on these actions being only שבות (רבנן-level), lighter than slaughtering, which is a תורה-level מלאכה. If the wart case were cutting with a tool, it would be a תורה-level מלאכה, and his argument would not work. So the משנה in פסחים must be speaking of רבנן-level actions, and the hand-versus-tool answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Slaughtering (here, of the קרבן פסח)
A שבת prohibition made by the רבנן
Torah-level forbidden labor

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the רבנן about the halacha. But the point here is only how he describes these actions: as שבות. Both sides of that dispute agree the actions are only רבנן-level.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected:
Rabbi Eliezer said: it is a fortiori:
If slaughtering, which is forbidden as a Torah labor,
overrides Shabbat,
these, which are forbidden only as a rabbinic decree,
is it not logical that they should override Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 17's claim that the listed cases are Torah-level
steps.kashyaTarget: The hand-versus-tool reading of the משנה in פסחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר calls all these actions שבות, so the wart case cannot be cutting with a tool (a Torah-level מלאכה)

steps.title: Both are by hand: the place makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new answer. Both משניות speak of cutting by hand. A שבות for the מקדש done inside the מקדש was permitted. A שבות for the מקדש done out in the country was not permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: both speak of cutting by hand. A שבות for the מקדש done inside the מקדש, the רבנן permitted. A שבות for the מקדש done in the country, they did not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the hand-versus-tool answer has fallen, רב יוסף gives a new way to fit the two משניות together. The difference is where the action is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are a רבנן-level שבות, cutting by hand. Our משנה speaks about inside the מקדש, where the רבנן allowed a שבות for the service. The משנה in פסחים speaks about the קרבן פסח being prepared out in the country, before reaching the מקדש. There, even a שבות for the מקדש's needs stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that (both cases)
By hand
The Temple
The country, outside the מקדש
They (the רבנן) permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's answer: both משניות speak of cutting by hand. A שבות for the מקדש is permitted inside the מקדש, but not out in the country.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule: the leniency for a שבות in the מקדש depends on location. It applies inside the מקדש, not just to anything done for the מקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Both this and that are by hand,
and a rabbinic decree for the Temple, in the Temple, they permitted;
a rabbinic decree for the Temple, in the country, they did not permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא וְהָא בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected hand-versus-tool answer with a new resolution based on location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות differ because of hand versus tool
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are by hand; a שבות is permitted inside the מקדש but not in the country

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges with the holy scroll on the threshold
steps.stepSummary: After אביי repeats רב יוסף's rule, רב ספרא brings a משנה. Someone reading a holy scroll on a threshold may roll it back if it slips out of his hand. This looks like a שבות for the מקדש done out in the country that is still permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי sat and repeated this teaching. רב ספרא challenged אביי: 'If someone was reading a scroll while sitting on the threshold, and the scroll rolled out of his hand, he may roll it back to himself.' But this is a שבות connected to holy things, done out in the country. Yet we do not make a גזירה that maybe it will fall all the way and he will come to carry it in!
steps.whatsHappening: The first line sets the scene: אביי is teaching רב יוסף's rule to others. Then רב ספרא attacks that rule with a משנה about a holy scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said a שבות for the מקדש is only permitted inside the מקדש. A holy scroll is treated like a holy, מקדש-type matter, and this case happens at home, out 'in the country.' Even so, the רבנן allow rolling it back and do not worry he will come to carry it, so a שבות of this type seems permitted outside the מקדש too.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling (here, רב יוסף's rule)
Threshold or doorstep
A רבנן-level prohibition, connected to holy things, being done outside the מקדש
We make a protective decree (גזירה)

phrases.english: Abaye sat and was saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: The teaching is רב יוסף's rule from Step 19.

phrases.english: Rav Safra challenged Abaye:
If one was reading a scroll on the threshold,
and the scroll rolled out of his hand —
phrases.notes: He is still holding one end.

phrases.english: he may roll it back to himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דִּשְׁבוּת דְּמִקְדָּשׁ בַּמְּדִינָה הוּא,
phrases.english: But here it is a rabbinic prohibition of a holy matter, done in the country,
and yet we do not decree
lest it fall and he come to carry it in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's new distinction from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that a שבות for the מקדש was not permitted out in the country.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A holy scroll is treated as a מקדש-type matter, and it may be rolled back outside the מקדש without any גזירה. So this kind of שבות is permitted out in the country.

steps.title: The threshold case is not a שבות at all
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the scroll משנה was already explained as a threshold that is a כרמלית, with the public domain in front of it. Since he holds one end of the scroll, there is not even a שבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we already explain that משנה as speaking of a threshold that is a כרמלית, with the public street passing in front of it? Since the end of the scroll is still tied in his hand, there is not even a שבות here!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב יוסף. He says the scroll case does not belong to the category of 'a שבות for holy things outside the מקדש' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The threshold is only a כרמלית, so even bringing something into it from the public domain is a רבנן-level problem, not a Torah-level one. On top of that, he still holds one end of the scroll, so rolling it back is not even a שבות. With no שבות in the case, it cannot prove anything about permitting a שבות outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: We established (explained) the case as
An in-between area that is only a רבנן-level domain
The public domain
Its end is tied to (held in) his hand

phrases.english: Didn't we establish it as a threshold that is a karmelit
with the public domain passing in front of it,
since its end is held in his hand —
there is not even a rabbinic prohibition?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's first challenge by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case redefinition: the case has no שבות at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rolling the scroll back is a permitted שבות done outside the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a כרמלית, while he holds the end, there is no שבות, so this משנה says nothing about a שבות for the מקדש.

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges with the קרבן פסח lowered into the oven
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא brings a second משנה: the קרבן פסח may be lowered into the oven just before שבת begins. The רבנן do not worry that he will stir the coals, even though this happens outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him again: 'We may lower the פסח into the oven just as it gets dark.' But this is a שבות for the מקדש done out in the country, and still we do not make a גזירה that maybe he will stir the coals!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא tries a second source against רב יוסף's rule. This time the case is the קרבן פסח being roasted outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary meat, the רבנן worry that someone who puts it in the oven right before שבת will stir the coals on שבת to speed up the cooking. For the פסח they do not make this גזירה, even though it is roasted at home, outside the מקדש. That looks like a שבות for the מקדש being permitted out in the country.

keyTerms.meaning: We lower (into the oven)
The קרבן פסח
Just as it gets dark (right before Shabbos)
He will stir the coals (a Torah-level מלאכה)

phrases.english: He challenged him: We may lower the Pesach offering
into the oven just as it gets dark.
But here it is a rabbinic prohibition of the Temple, in the country,
and yet we do not decree lest he stir the coals!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לְתַנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is answered, רב ספרא brings a second, stronger challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that a שבות for the מקדש was not permitted out in the country.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרבן פסח is a מקדש matter, roasted outside the מקדש, and the רבנן skip their usual גזירה. So a שבות for the מקדש is permitted outside it.

steps.title: אביי is silent; רב יוסף answers that a פסח group is careful
steps.stepSummary: אביי has no answer. When he reports the challenge to רב יוסף, רב יוסף asks why he did not answer that the members of a פסח group are careful people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was silent. When he came before רב יוסף, he said to him: 'This is what רב ספרא said to me.' רב יוסף said to him: 'Why didn't you answer him: the members of a פסח group are careful!'
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא tells us that אביי could not answer the second challenge. Then רב יוסף himself gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The group eating a קרבן פסח is focused and careful about their מצוה, so there is no real fear that they will stir the coals. That is why the רבנן made no גזירה here. It is a special reason that applies only to this case, so רב יוסף's general rule still stands: a שבות for the מקדש is not permitted out in the country.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
You answer (give a תירוץ)
Members of the group sharing one קרבן פסח
Careful, alert, and eager

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's rule survives both challenges. The scroll case has no שבות at all. The פסח case has a special reason: the group is careful. So a שבות for the מקדש is permitted only inside the מקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying that a שבות for the מקדש is permitted out in the country. He is saying the פסח case never needed a גזירה in the first place, because careful people are not likely to stir the coals.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) was silent.
When he came before Rav Yosef,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר לִי רַב סָפְרָא.
phrases.english: he said to him: This is what Rav Safra said to me.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תְּשַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He said to him: Why didn't you answer him:
Members of the Pesach group are careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's second challenge from Step 22, after אביי's silence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-reason distinction: the case has its own reason for no גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח case shows that a שבות for the מקדש is permitted outside the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: No גזירה was needed because the פסח group is careful. The general rule against a שבות for the מקדש out in the country remains.

steps.title: Why אביי did not accept the 'careful people' answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains אביי's position. We say that כהנים are careful people, but we do not say that the members of a פסח group are careful people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He holds that we say 'כהנים are careful,' but we do not say 'members of a פסח group are careful.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי did not give the answer רב יוסף suggested. In אביי's view, only כהנים can be trusted to be careful. Ordinary people in a פסח group cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף wanted to say that the פסח group will not stir the coals because they are careful people. אביי disagrees. כהנים work in the מקדש all the time and are trained to be careful. Regular people who joined together for one קרבן פסח do not have that training, so we would still worry that they might forget and stir the coals.

keyTerms.meaning: Careful, alert people. They can be trusted not to slip up.
The priests who do the service in the מקדש
The members of a group who signed up together for one קרבן פסח
We say (we apply this reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that אביי is calling the פסח group careless or bad. He only means that they lack the trained alertness of כהנים, so the רבנן's normal worry still applies to them.

phrases.english: And Abaye? 'Priests are careful' — this we say,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking why אביי did not answer this way, and then gives his reason.

phrases.english: 'Members of a Pesach group are careful' — this we do not say.
phrases.notes: Regular people are not used to the constant alertness of the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why אביי did not use the answer רב יוסף proposed in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the 'careful people' reasoning to כהנים only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that anyone busy with a קרבן, like a פסח group, is trusted to be careful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only כהנים, who are trained in the מקדש, get the presumption of being careful. A פסח group does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב יוסף's approach still faces the problem of the קרבן פסח in the oven, at least for אביי. This opens the door for רבא's new answer.

steps.title: רבא resolves the contradiction using רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה that allows cutting the wart follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that the preparations for a מצוה push aside שבת. רבי אליעזר also agrees that if the act can be done in a changed way, we change it. So it is done by hand, not with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who said that the preparations for a מצוה push aside שבת. And רבי אליעזר agrees that as much as we are able to do things differently, we do them differently.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a brand-new answer to the clash between the two משניות about cutting a wart. He says they follow different תנאים: the lenient משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that whatever must be done to make a מצוה possible may be done on שבת. Cutting a wart off a קרבן is one example, since a קרבן with a wart cannot be brought. But he also agrees that we should change the normal way of doing the act whenever possible, to remember it is שבת. That is why the משנה allows cutting by hand, a less serious way, and not with a tool.

keyTerms.meaning: The preparations needed to make a מצוה possible
Push aside (override) the laws of Shabbos
And he agrees (concedes)
To do it differently, in an unusual way

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer: the משנה that allows cutting a wart follows רבי אליעזר (preparations for a מצוה override שבת). Even רבי אליעזר requires doing the act in a changed way when possible, so it is done by hand and not with a tool.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר allows the act in any way at all. Even though he lets the preparation override שבת, he still insists on the changed, lighter method (by hand) whenever one is available.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא no longer splits the case into 'inside the מקדש' versus 'out in the country' like רב יוסף did. Instead, he explains the contradiction as a disagreement between תנאים, and this avoids the challenges רב ספרא raised.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It (this Mishnah) is Rabbi Eliezer's view,
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה that permits cutting the wart.

And Rabbi Eliezer agrees

phrases.notes: This is why the cutting is done by hand, not with a tool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב יוסף and אביי discussion behind and offers a completely different resolution of the original contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משניות to different תנאים (the lenient one follows רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both משניות shared one view, so we needed a distinction like 'in the מקדש' versus 'in the country.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה permitting the cutting follows רבי אליעזר, who allows preparations for a מצוה on Shabbos but requires a changed method (by hand) when possible.
